title: Adaptive residency window planner for extended-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Define and ship an adaptive 'residency window' planner that places per-layer KV residency and compaction thresholds optimized for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen variants under extended-context workloads (>=32k tokens).

Motivation: Current static residency heuristics cause either excessive GPU memory retention during bursty long-context sessions or expensive recomputation when we evict too aggressively. For multi-tenant and bursty streaming workloads, we need a model-aware planner that: (1) predicts layer-level hotness, (2) selects kernel families with residency hints, and (3) adapts compaction thresholds to workload phase (inference vs. sustained generation). This should reduce peak working set and improve sustained throughput while preserving tail latency SLOs.

Scope & Deliverables:
- Offline profiler that collects per-layer access frequency and KV hit-rate over simulated multi-session workloads for Llama-2-70B, Mistral-8x, and Qwen-14B-long.
- Residency window planner service (planner v1) that outputs: per-model, per-variant residency windows, compaction thresholds, and kernel hint flags.
- Integration: runtime to consume planner outputs and (a) apply per-request residency hints, (b) trigger a background compaction policy when pressure > threshold, and (c) expose diagnostics to Console.
- Acceptance criteria: peak GPU memory usage reduced by >=10% for heavy long-context workloads (>=32k tokens) without increasing 99th-percentile latency by >5%; nightly regression tests added to perf-suite.

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive compaction reduces memory but can trigger recomputation (kv reload) which hurts end-to-end latency. We selected a conservative hysteresis window where compaction is only allowed once a layer's inactivity exceeds 2x median inter-access for the session type.
- Per-layer residency windows are computed using an exponential moving average of access inter-arrival times combined with a variant-specific multiplier (learned from offline traces). This trades tunability for simplicity vs. a full RL approach.
- Kernel selection hints are best-effort and non-blocking; when the planner prefers a low-footprint kernel it sets a hint but runtime may override if latency-critical (per-route) flags are present.

Acceptance tests and metrics:
- Perf microbench harness: 3 model variants x 5 workload mixes (single long stream, multi-tenant interleaved, bursty short-then-long, prompt-heavy prefix reuse, conversation-like alternation). Compare: baseline static residency vs. planner v1.
- Metrics: peak GPU memory (MiB), average throughput (tokens/s), 95/99 latency, KV reload count per session, GC/compaction time, cost per 1M tokens extrapolated.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: small percentage of Hosted API traffic routed to planner v1 on dedicated pool. Monitor memory and latency changes for 48h.
- Escalation: auto-fallback to static residency profiles if KV reload count increases >30% vs baseline or 99th P99 latency regresses >7%.
- Full: staged rollout to all Dedicated pools after 2 successful canaries and sign-off from SRE.

Open questions:
- How often should the planner re-evaluate residency windows during a very long session (>=100k tokens)? Current plan: every 10k tokens or when memory pressure crosses 85% GPU.
- Should we expose per-customer residency overrides (enterprise controls) in Private deployments? Initial stance: allow opt-in via Dedicated config, gated behind security review.

Links to artifacts:
- Profiler design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Residency+Window+Profiler+Design
- Perf dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/runtime/memory-profiles
comments: 2025-02-15 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff notes. Ran sampling profiler on Mistral-8x with synthetic streaming workload. Observed layer 10-18 have 3x higher access persistence for convish heads. Created initial CSV traces in GCS: gs://redwood-perf/ENG-760401/mistral-traces-20250215.zip

2025-02-20 - Brian Chen: Implemented initial EMA-based hotness estimator and produced residency curves for Llama-2-70B at seq_len 64k. Peak working set reduced ~12% in single-tenant long-stream test, but KV reloads increased by 18% under bursty interleaved workload. Included plots in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4872

2025-02-24 - Priya Singh (SRE): Observed a modest increase in background compaction IO during the Mistral canary. Recommendation: add global compaction rate limit and a per-device backoff window to avoid interfering with NIC/GPU scheduler. Filed follow-up task ENG-760412.

2025-03-01 - Lina Patel (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria. Emphasize customer regression thresholds and add a cost-savings target for runway teams (>=8% per-token cost reduction in Dedicated). Also requested a small UX surface in Console to flag sessions where planner auto-evicted heavy KV blocks.

2025-03-03 - Brian Chen: Benchmarks v1 across three variants completed. Summary: Mistral-8x long-stream peak memory -15%, throughput +9%; Llama-2-70B peak memory -11%, throughput +7%; Qwen-14B-long peak memory -13%, throughput +5%. 99th latency change within +3%. Draft PR with planner config and unit tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4921

2025-03-05 - Marco Rossi (Infra): Reviewed kernel-hint integration. Suggested making hint flags additive so future kernel families can be trialed without planner changes. Also requested telemetry keys to be stable before rollout (planner.window_v1 => planner.window_v1_beta).
next_steps: 1) Merge planner config PR and land unit/integration tests. 2) Add compaction rate limiter (ENG-760412). 3) Start canary on a small hosted GPU pool for 48h. 4) Add Console flagging and telemetry namespacing. 5) Post-mortem and decision doc for whether to advance to planner v2 with RL-based scheduling.
owner_notes: We should prioritize Mistral variant tuning first (best win/effort ratio) and keep Llama/Qwen configs conservative until we collect more 64k+ session traces. Keep P0 for any rollout regression that increases P99 latency >7%.
